svg.data-what: the spinal cord cut across, its back (dorsal side) at the top, right and left as in the picture: grey matter butterfly, white matter, roots, ganglia and meninges

ellipse.data-what: the subarachnoid space, filled with cerebrospinal fluid, between the arachnoid and the pia that clings to the cord

path.data-what: the spinal nerve on the right, where sensory and motor fibres travel together to the body
the dorsal root on the right, bringing sensory fibres into the dorsal horn
the ventral root on the right, carrying motor fibres out from the ventral horn to the muscles

g.data-what: the dorsal root ganglion on the right, holding the cell bodies of the sensory neurons

path.data-what: the spinal nerve on the left, where sensory and motor fibres travel together to the body
the dorsal root on the left, bringing sensory fibres into the dorsal horn
the ventral root on the left, carrying motor fibres out from the ventral horn to the muscles

g.data-what: the dorsal root ganglion on the left, holding the cell bodies of the sensory neurons

path.data-what: the white matter, columns of myelinated fibres running up and down the cord: dorsal, lateral and ventral columns
the dorsal columns, white matter carrying fine touch, vibration and the sense of position up to the brain
the grey matter, the butterfly of neuron cell bodies and synapses in the middle of the cord
the dorsal horns of the grey matter, where sensory fibres arrive and pain signals are first relayed
the ventral horns, holding the motor neurons whose axons leave to command the muscles

circle.data-what: the central canal, a thin channel of cerebrospinal fluid running the length of the cord
the anterior spinal artery, running in the front groove of the cord

path.data-what: the dura mater, the tough outer membrane of the meninges wrapping the cord and the roots
